metadata.protocol: repl-from-stdin NDJSON: Initialize, Evaluate, GetSeed; one process, isolated initialization per case
metadata.policy: Go follows the TypeScript reference for seeded sampling, traversal, domain limits and diagnostics; modulo-by-zero deliberately returns a structured QNT503. Raw Rust values and traces are preserved.

cases.name: division
cases.reason: Both references truncate integer division toward zero.

cases.name: negative-division
cases.reason: Negative division truncates toward zero.

cases.name: negative-remainder
cases.reason: Remainder follows the dividend sign.

cases.name: past-i64
cases.reason: Current Rust uses BigInt fallback; arithmetic is not limited to i64.

cases.name: large-power
cases.reason: Arbitrary precision arithmetic agrees.

cases.name: large-literal-wire
cases.reason: Rust IR transports large integer literals as decimal strings.

cases.name: short-circuit
cases.reason: Both references skip the failing branch.

cases.name: division-zero
cases.reason: Both references report QNT503.

cases.name: remainder-zero
cases.reason: The TypeScript evaluator wraps the builtin RangeError as QNT501; Go deliberately reports Rust-compatible QNT503.

cases.name: zero-power-zero
cases.reason: Both references reject undefined powers.

cases.name: negative-exponent
cases.reason: Both references reject negative integer exponents.

cases.name: empty-head
cases.reason: Both references reject an empty head.

cases.name: out-of-range-index
cases.reason: Both references reject an invalid index; messages can differ.

cases.name: large-interval
cases.reason: Go follows TypeScript arbitrary precision interval bounds; Rust rejects bounds outside i64 with QNT601.

err.message: Interval bounds must fit in 64-bit integers in the Rust backend: 18446744073709551616.to(18446744073709551618)

cases.name: large-cardinality
cases.reason: Go follows TypeScript exact cardinality; Rust caps cardinality and reports QNT601.

err.message: Integer overflow in cardinality computation: powerset size 2^80 exceeds the maximum supported size

cases.name: infinite-cardinality
cases.reason: Go follows TypeScript QNT514; Rust reports non-enumerability as QNT501.

cases.name: set-order-small
cases.reason: Set equality is extensional; the separate fold case captures runtime iteration.

cases.name: set-order-hashed
cases.reason: Serialized set order differs; observable fold cases distinguish iteration from canonical serialization.

cases.name: map-order
cases.reason: Map equality is extensional; serialized entry order and runtime key iteration are checked separately.

cases.name: observable-set-order
cases.reason: A fold exposes runtime iteration order, independently of value serialization.

cases.name: observable-map-order
cases.reason: Map key iteration follows the selected backend.

cases.name: seeded-interval
cases.reason: Go reproduces TypeScript Squares32 draws; Rust uses rand64 modulo the bound.

cases.name: seeded-set
cases.reason: Seeded values depend on both RNG algorithm and set traversal order.

cases.name: seeded-wide-interval
cases.reason: TypeScript consumes two counter words at bound 2^32; Rust consumes one.

cases.name: seed-counter-limit
cases.source: { nondet p=5.to(8).oneOf(); nondet q=5.to(8).oneOf(); q::debug("p",p)==p and q::debug("q",q)==q }
cases.reason: TypeScript wraps its counter modulo 2^64; Rust saturates at u64::MAX.
